best_for: Developers and designers who keep their code on GitHub and want commits, branches and pull request checkouts without learning Git commands.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: GitHub Desktop is MIT-licensed and free. You can install it without an account and sign in to GitHub or GitHub Enterprise when you want to.

points.title: Made for GitHub, fine elsewhere
points.text: It works with other Git hosts, but it is built around GitHub. Signing in to GitHub needs no separate credential manager, and you can check out a pull request without a browser.

points.title: Tidy commits by hand
points.text: You pick which changed lines go into a commit, add co-authors, and drag commits to cherry-pick, squash or reorder them.

points.title: No official Linux build
points.text: GitHub says Linux is not supported. The Flatpak here is a community fork by shiftkey, not marked verified on Flathub, and was at 3.4.13 when Windows was at 3.7.0.

points.title: Two ways to install on Windows
points.text: It needs 64-bit Windows 10 or later. The .exe installs per user. The MSI is for admins: deployed by Group Policy, it installs the app for each user at their next sign-in. Builds come for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Older versions on Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 78 versions. macOS has Intel and Apple silicon zips but lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
